root_cause.text: In `damos_walk()`, the function assigns a caller-provided stack-allocated control structure pointer to `ctx->walk_control` before verifying the DAMON context is running, and fails to clear this pointer on the error path when the context is inactive, leaving a dangling pointer that can lead to use-after-free or permanent -EBUSY.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "damos_walk() sets ctx->walk_control to the caller-provided control structure before checking whether the context is running. If the context is inactive ... the function returns -EINVAL without clearing ctx->walk_control. This leaves a dangling pointer to a stack-allocated structure that will be freed when the caller returns." The patch adds a cleanup block: `mutex_lock(&ctx->walk_control_lock); if (ctx->walk_control == control) ctx->walk_control = NULL; mutex_unlock(&ctx->walk_control_lock);` before returning -EINVAL, mirroring the fix pattern from commit f9132fbc2e83.
